# Bohm and Krishnamurti — Truth, Actuality, and the Limits of Thought (18 May 1975)

## Bibliographic identity

Primary transcript hosted by Krishnamurti Foundation Trust. Before final citation, record the page's displayed title/revision date and stable media identifier; use transcript paragraph/time locators rather than inventing pagination.

## Essay use

Primary dialogue for observer/observed, truth/reality, and Bohm's recollection of a spinning wheel with a “thread running straight.” The image supports the complex-plane/artistic discussion of a movement that runs true through transformation.

**Passages needed:** exact context of the wheel/thread image; observer/observed; truth and reality; limits of thought.

**Claim boundary:** the complex modulus/thread alignment is the essay's mathematical interpretation. Preserve the source's exact image—thread, not a belt—and the dialogue's context.

<a id="bohm-krishnamurti-1975-05-18-dialogue-q002"></a>
### q002 · concluding exchanges on knowledge and reality

Thought can mistake its own reflexive activity for an independently existing object. The speakers explore correcting that independence claim while retaining functional knowledge. Krishnamurti questions Bohm's account of energy and their common root; their formulations must retain that disagreement.

**Locator:** concluding exchanges on knowledge and reality.
